claims.text: An integrated machine-learning framework combining high-throughput measurements with chemical-disorder descriptors can accurately predict HEAs with exceptionally low lattice thermal conductivity.
The proposed framework will outperform traditional predictive models by at least approximately 20%.
The target HEAs are compositionally disordered in their as-synthesized state.
Chemical disorder plays a dominant role in phonon scattering in the target HEAs.
The predictive intervention uses high-throughput experimental data and chemical-disorder descriptors to model phonon transport.
The intended operating range extends from near-ambient to moderately elevated temperatures.
Phonon transport is the dominant heat-conduction mechanism over the intended operating range.
The degree of chemical disorder can be represented using configurational entropy and local-atomic-environment indicators.
Greater chemical disorder increases phonon scattering and reduces phonon mean free path.
Linking disorder descriptors to measured phonon-transport properties allows machine learning to capture complex structure-property relationships.
Conventional predictive methods oversimplify the effect of chemical disorder on phonon transport.
The ML model will identify HEA compositions whose measured phonon thermal conductivity is at least approximately 20% below values predicted by traditional models.
A measured conductivity below a traditional model's prediction indicates that the ML model is more accurate.
The baseline consists of conventional ab initio and empirical predictions.
The approach is primarily applicable when phonons dominate heat conduction.
Significant phase transformations may reduce the effectiveness of the approach.
Non-phononic heat-conduction mechanisms may reduce the effectiveness of the approach.
The magnitude of predictive improvement depends on dataset quality, dataset extent, and the selected disorder descriptors.
Time-domain thermoreflectance and scattering-based mean-free-path characterization can provide the experimental measurements needed to test the hypothesis.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement of at least approximately 20% over traditional predictions would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims improved prediction accuracy, but the predicted outcome and falsification rule assess whether measured conductivity is lower than traditional-model predictions. A lower measured value does not by itself establish that the ML prediction has smaller error; accuracy requires direct comparison of ML and baseline prediction errors against the same measurements.

The design specifies separate ML-selected and traditional-model-selected composition sets, whereas the rule compares measurements with traditional-model predictions. It does not clearly define a matched-composition comparison or an error metric for the two models.
